q1.answer: No. ADR013 ('Proper use of HTTP fetching libraries', the node-fetch one) is marked superseded and no longer applies. It was replaced by ADR014, which says frontend plugins/packages should prefer the fetchApiRef (as this file does via its injected fetchApi), while Node.js code should use native fetch instead of node-fetch.

q2.answer: ADR007 ('Use MSW to mock http requests') requires any fetch/XMLHTTPRequest in tests to be mocked with msw. It frames this as replacing a world where every test (unit through e2e) 'always have their own implementation of mocking these requests', so the msw approach avoids each test inventing its own ad-hoc mocking scheme and avoids mocking fetch/XHR directly (brittle, implementation-coupled), using an express-style route declaration instead.

q3.answer: ADR006 cites two technical problems with React.FC: it implicitly adds a `children` prop even when not wanted, and it does not support a generic type on children. The concrete upstream fact given is that Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript template because it was found to be an unnecessary feature with next to no benefits.

q4.answer: ADR010 mandates Luxon as the replacement for Moment.js. Two reasons given for retiring Moment.js: it suffers from large bundle sizes and mutable state issues, and separately, the Moment.js project itself is 'being sunset' with its maintainers recommending a move to a more modern alternative library.

q5.answer: ADR004 ('Module Export Structure') requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way to the package root src/index.ts (each index file only re-exporting its own immediate directory children). It was written specifically to make it easy to answer questions like 'Is the export in this module also exported by the package?' / 'What is exported from this directory?'.

q6.answer: No, they are not part of the public API. Under ADR004's rule, a symbol is only publicly exported if it can be traced upward through a chain of index.ts files to the package root; since there is no src/utils/index.ts and src/index.ts doesn't mention these files, the chain is broken at the very first step, so notificationLinks.ts and plainText.ts are implicitly private even though nothing explicitly marks them as such.

q7.answer: ADR011 says an `x-react` package is for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. For notifications to need a notifications-react package, there would have to be components/hooks in this plugin that other, third-party frontend plugins also want to reuse/depend on -- i.e. shared frontend code crossing plugin boundaries, which currently doesn't exist here (everything stays internal to the single `notifications` package).

q8.answer: ADR003 allows a default export only when 'absolutely necessary', giving React.lazy-loaded modules as the one example (React.lazy expects a module with a default export). The workaround it gives for avoiding even that exception is to wrap the dynamic import and remap the named export to `default` in the `.then()`, e.g. `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the `loader`/`component` option pattern for providing JSX elements and components. Its Consequences section says they will update all APIs for the new frontend system (`@backstage/frontend-*` packages) but will NOT update any of the existing APIs for the old frontend system (`@backstage/core-*` packages) -- i.e. they explicitly do not plan to retrofit the pattern onto pre-existing old-style code like the dev app.
